RageFestival

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We go to Umhlanga to find out what thousands of matriculants get up to during Rage madness

Summary:
10 days of outrageous partying - at the clubs, on the beaches, at the outdoor Sound Factory. Every year thousands of matriculants flock to the Rage Festival on the KZN north coast. It;s about freedom, it;s about fun and a whole lot more. What really happens at this once in a lifetime experience?

Script:


RAGE FESTIVAL

V/O: At high schools all over Joburg the matrics are writing their last exam. Freedom is only hours away. Soon they will go from this – to this, because the end of matric means the beginning of Rage and a parent’s worse nightmare. But what really goes on?

Claire: It’s the big opening night of the matric Rage festival called the Sound Factory, just outside Kings Park stadium, and over twenty thousand teenagers are expected to attend.

Greg: The actual experience of being at Rage is 9 days, 80 events.

V/O: Greg Walsh is a former banker, and Rage has been his baby for the last 12 years.

Greg: Our first parties were actually at a nightclub called Cloud Nine in Umhlanga and I think we had about 200 people per party.

V/O: Now over 20 000 youngsters fly to Durban every year and descend on the coastal playground. At the airport they get their Rage passports – an all access ticket that costs anything from R900 to R4000.

Greg: There are different tiers of tickets: there’s a Regular ticket, a Platinum pass and a Rage Black pass that gives them different levels of VIP treatment and access. On the back end of it though it’s also an NFC enabled wearable, which locks onto their wrist.

V/O: NFC or Near Field Communication allows for electronic communication over short distances.

Greg: They then go and register that ticket with their ID number and a really comprehensive registration – it takes them about half an hour online, and out of that we get their full information, contact details, their next of kin – we get 2 next of kin, medical aid information.

V/O: It’s the next best thing to chipping your kid.
They stay in the resort towns of Ballito and Umhlanga – the Sodom and Gomorrah of every parent’s imagination. There have been rumours of serious problems in the past, but these remain unconfirmed. We found a carnival atmosphere in the streets, and happy kids brimming with excitement.

Claire: And how long have you been planning to be coming here?

Kids: Over a year. Ja, since like September last year. We had to buy all our passes and book in at the hotel like a year ago.

Claire: May I ask how much money you’ve spent just to get to Rage?

Girl: About R7500 just to get here.

V/O: In Ballito they take over La Montagne Resort, and in Umhlanga the Cabana Beach Resort and the Umhlanga Sands Hotel. For the next 7 days – and nights - these massive establishments will be entirely populated by teenagers, with no parental interference.

Gareth: No I’ll definitely have an incredible time. You know that, I know that.

V/O: While they wait to check in, the drinks are flowing and expectations are high.

Niks: What happens in this place is more than I myself have ever seen.

Claire: So what are you expecting for the next few days?

Costa: Craziness.

Claire: What’s craziness?

Boy: Say what you really mean.

Costa: Girls, alcohol…don’t say the last one, don’t say the last one!

Claire: Say the last one!

Costa: No it’s alcohol and girls basically.

Boy: I’m going to bed, reading my Bible, having a beer with my friends.

Niks: This is more than what they think it is. This is way more than what they think it is.

Claire: What is it?

Niks: It’s greatness.

V/O: And witnessing the greatness are a few Moms waiting to register their kids.

Claire: How do you feel about leaving him here after you’ve checked him in?

Aunt: You know if you haven’t prepared your children well before, it’s a bit too late when they get to 18.

Renee: We all panic and pray for the best.

Heather: You must embrace it and enjoy – and it’s fun!

V/O: It seems every precaution is taken to keep the kids safe.

Greg: Ideally don’t arrive with a vehicle; you don’t need a vehicle. Buy your Rage Ride tokens so you can use the Rage Ride shuttles. Or if you’re up in Ballito use the Rage Rail. It’s a brand new thing we did this year, actioned on the back of a suggestion from the Ballito SAPS. They had a private train that we could make use of so we could kit it out, make it a DJ train with drinking carts etc, we have our own security on board.

V/O: The train takes them all the way to the Moses Mabhida Station in Durban, which is a short walk from the Sound Factory. Everyone has to tap in at the gates, so the organizers know exactly who’s arrived. Once inside, security is actually tightened.

Greg: As a festival we’ve got an absolute zero tolerance to drugs policy. We also have about 30 to 40 undercover cops every single night. They literally look like the Ragers.

V/O: Four dance floors offer the latest lighting and sound technology, with local and international DJs.

Sfx: Music

V/O: Outside the celebrations are in full swing as well.

Claire: Guys how are you guys going to keep on drinking and still keep standing?

Guy 1: Hey come for the interview bru. It’s an interview, we’re famous.

Guy 2: Check it’s an Oreo, an Oreo!

Claire: And where are you from?

Guy 2: Wait! Take a photo of the Oreo!

Brodie: We’ve been waiting for this for 5 years.

Claire: Five years?

Brodie: Five long years. It’s finally here; it’s living, it’s happening, it’s good.

Claire: And you came to find?

Girl 1: Men!…

Girl 2: And listen to great, amazing music by great DJs.

Girl 1: But hot guys – Number 1 hot guys.

V/O: The hot guys were cooling down in the bar area with a lot of liquid refreshments.
And when they’ve had too much, the Red Frogs jump in.

Paul: We’re a group of volunteers from all over the country. We really come down to Rage, and 5 locations around the country to safeguard this generation of young people, to be a positive presence here, and really to support them trough what can be quite an emotionally and physically confronting time.

V/O: But some need more support than others. The emergency services are on site to catch those kids who have gone way above their own tolerance levels.

Werner: We will stabilize them on site, we’ve got a full resuscitation bay inside the medical clinic, and then from here our ambulance is parked just next to the tent. We will take the patient through to the closest hospital.

V/O: We went to Umhlanga Hospital and found that two Ragers had been admitted to High Care with alcohol poisoning that weekend. But the vast majority stay on their feet and dance until 1am when the Sound Factory closes, and the crowd moves on to the clubs for the after-parties. Those last until 4am, and then they catch a shuttle back to the hotels to watch the sunrise.

Claire: What happened last night?

Guy: Ooh, last night was intense.

Claire: Tell me about the girls?

Guy 1: That’s a hot topic. They’re stuck up though, we don’t know why? What’s wrong, why you got to be so stuck up?

Claire: What do you mean, they don’t want to talk to you guys?

Guy 1: No. We’re like hey, and they’re like why are you talking to me? It’s weird.

Guy 2: They need to become more like you and speak to us more often.

V/O: By 6am, the hotel is deserted. When most holidaymakers would normally be getting up to enjoy the day, the Ragers have just gone to bed.

V/O: But by midday they’ve bounced back. It’s the afternoon pool party, and time to show off your pecs and packs. The place is heaving with hormones - sun’s out, gun’s out.

Tebogo: What can I say I’m still drunk. I woke up drunk and I’m still drunk. And I’m going to be drunk for a whole week. Sorry Mom, I’m sorry.

Claire: What was your favourite part?

Dean: The women, the women.

Claire: Really? Hot girls?

Dean: Ah hot! Only mint chicks hey, the birds were so on form last night I didn’t know what to do with myself.

Claire: But you say the talent is lacking?

Girl 1: Ja but hopefully tonight it will be fine.

Girl 2: We couldn’t find that many good-looking boys, but we’ll keep looking. They pop out.

Tebogo: I pulled 4 girls last night. It’s my free weekend birthday, what can I say, my birthday month.

Claire: Are you just trying to impress us?

Tebogo: No, honest 4 girls.

Claire: And then what do you do with those 4 girls?

Tebogo: They went home to sleep.

Claire: Are you man enough for 4 girls?

Tebogo: Of course, I’m small, but what can I say? If your game’s good what can I say?

V/O: But with all the drinking, how much sex is actually happening?

Dean: You have to have this band to get back into the hotel room.

Claire: No one is partying in the rooms, there’s no craziness on the floors?

Dean: Nothing, no they are really, really strict, in every aspect.

V/O: Without the wristband we couldn’t get access to the rooms, but undercover footage showed very little action.

Gareth: We put out every bit of safe and responsible messaging that we can. Can we control their behavior when they close the door and we’re no longer there? That is unfortunately out of our control.

V/O: But do the Ragers have it under control?

Claire: Are you stocking extra condoms?

Alwyn: Unfortunately yes – many, many condoms. But I suppose it’s better to be safe than sorry, hey?

Claire link: So what’s crucial to survive the week at Rage? Sunblock. All the drinking is going on, you have to protect your liver, so key ok. You need to get the condoms, crucial, ticket to fun – that’s what that is – no access if you’re not going to do it. Return ticket – another pack just for variation; And this is when an oopsie happens – morning after pill – apparently they get sold out, so you never know what’s going to happen in Rage week.

Girl: These are literally my Dad’s words – “Rage is designed so that you do not get out alive” – his exact words. So they think Rage is just drugs, alcohol and sex I suppose.

Claire: And then what it’s the truth behind Rage?

Girl 1: It is that stuff, but the truth is that you chose.

Girl 2: My parents were cool. I mean we waited twelve years – it was high school and primary school for this event. I wouldn’t miss it.

Claire: So what’s the best thing about Rage?

Dean: The best thing about Rage is that we don’t have old people here hey, no really like 25 year-old, 26-year-olds that think they like own the place. It’s just a whole bunch of 18 year-olds who come and have a sick time hey.

Claire link: Before coming to see what Rage really was about my initial reaction as a parent was that my son would never come here. But I’ve seen what the kids get up to and I’m pleasantly surprised. If I was 18, would I want to be here? Hell yes!
